paper.title_en: Metallic Néel order stabilized by coupling between inequivalent Hubbard layers
paper.abstract_en: Inspired by recent ARPES studies on multilayer ($n\geq3$ layers) cuprate superconductors, we use the unrestricted Hartree-Fock approximation to explore the ground-state phase diagram of two coupled, inequivalently doped square-lattice Hubbard layers. In the decoupled-layer limit, the lightly hole-doped ground state is typically an incommensurate spin-stripe state. However, with sufficiently strong interlayer coupling, stripe order is destabilized relative to a commensurate Néel-ordered metal. The resulting state exhibits a reconstructed Fermi surface with hole pockets centered at $(\pmπ/2,\pmπ/2)$ that are similar in character to those seen in experiments. Our results illustrate the qualitatively new physics that can arise from interlayer coupling in multilayer cuprates.
